title: Digital arrest scams - the new fraud everyone should know about
p1: Imagine getting a video call from someone claiming to be a police officer who says you're under "digital arrest" and must stay on the call until your case is cleared. It sounds unbelievable, yet people are losing their savings because they think hanging up will make things worse.
p2: The biggest misconception is that authorities can force you to stay on a video call, transfer money for "verification," or keep an investigation secret. They can't. Fraudsters use fake IDs, official-looking backgrounds, and legal jargon to create panic before you have time to think. The scam works because fear often overrides common sense.
p3: If anyone claims you're under digital arrest, pause instead of reacting. End the call, verify the claim using the official phone number of the agency involved, and never transfer money or share OTPs, banking details, or screen access. One simple habit can save you: never trust the phone number or documents shown during the call. Always verify independently using official sources.
conclusion: Before today, had you heard of the term "digital arrest," and what would be your first step if you received a call like this?
